purpose: Executable design oracles enforced by the accounting kernel conformance suite

cases.given: Two nonzero uniquely ordered postings in one book use exact typed values and balance in the functional commodity.
One same-book correction exactly negates the original journal and retains complete policy, evidence, and lineage.
A fully resolved typed command and complete dated policy snapshot are evaluated twice against identical book state.
Specific stable lot IDs select an available quantity and allocate exact rational total basis under an applicable transfer policy.
An active posting account has a unique chart code, an acyclic same-book parent, and an admissible commodity at the accounting date.
A later market observation produces a reporting valuation while transaction price, basis, and book value remain unchanged.
Two presentations of the same identified postings differ only in input order.
A new command matches the current expected revision and its complete canonical input has not been retained before.
A new zero-balance operational accrual book has an immutable identity, valid chart, calendar, and no opening journal.
Close pins one population and reopen appends disclosure while explicitly superseding every dependent later close.
All projections are deleted and rebuilt from the ordered canonical revision chain.
A posting selects one active same-book member for each dimension required by its applicable policy; another posting legitimately selects no optional dimensions.

Two genuinely committed raw journal/effect tuples have the same delimiter concatenation. The explicit structural profile resolves both original postings, while legacy replay preserves its original shadowed lookup. Durable round-trip and command retry preserve the original complete result hash and encoded history.

A book whose genesis configuration selected the chain-head state commitment activates and commits a journal. Its content hash is the typed commitment over its identity, counters, active configuration, opening boundary and revision chain head; the restored aggregate reproduces it and every collection; a book without the marker keeps its original complete-population hash.
A command contains binary floating input, a nonpositive rational denominator, or arithmetic beyond the admitted representation.
A market value or transaction price is supplied where canonical book value or cost basis is required.
Quantized functional book values differ by one minor unit and no explicit rounding posting is present.
A reversal changes only book values, crosses books, omits lineage, or independently corrects an already corrected effect.
A boundary service attempts to book a proposal with an omitted value or unresolved lot choice directly.
Command evaluation attempts a clock, network, authorization, random, or storage read not supplied in its input.
Two lots share date and label and a selector identifies them only by rendered attributes.
A disposal allocates more quantity or basis than the selected ordinary holdings contain.
A lot crosses a declared basis boundary without an applicable continuity or disposal-and-reacquisition policy.
A reporting valuation attempts to replace transaction price, basis, or booked value in canonical history.
Recording time is silently substituted for accounting date or policy-effective time.
A chart has duplicate codes, a parent cycle, a cross-book parent, an inactive account, or a forbidden commodity.
A journal contains duplicate posting identity or ordinal, zero value, virtual posting, unresolved posting, or fewer than two postings.
Equivalent identified postings produce different canonical hashes solely because source order changed.
The command result, intent, journal, provenance, or revision record cannot commit together.
An activated book changes owner, functional commodity, basis, calendar identity, or timezone in place.
A zero-balance activation includes a zero-value or otherwise fabricated opening journal.
Regular periods overlap, the accounting date resolves to no regular period, or a closed period does not admit the journal kind.
A retained command ID is submitted with different complete canonical content.
A rejection or replay consumes sequence, a revision skips, or a revision hash omits an ordered canonical effect.
An earlier period is reopened while a dependent later close remains presented as current without disclosure or supersession.
An incremental projection differs from a rebuild over the same canonical revision cutoff.
A posting omits a required dimension, selects two members on one axis, or references a wrong-book, inactive, unknown, cyclic, or duplicate-coded member.
A canonical identifier is empty, reused, dangling, ambiguous, or paired with conflicting content, or a digest omits its algorithm, canonicalization version, or complete typed object.

A state of a book with the chain-head state commitment carries a journal list that no longer equals the ordered revision effects and is re-sealed with its own commitment, which does not depend on that list; recovery proves the list against the chain and rejects it.
